events.description: All systems connecting to DynamoDB in us-east-1 via the public endpoint began experiencing DNS failures and failed to connect; global table replicas experienced prolonged replication lag to and from us-east-1.
EC2 DWFM state checks began to fail because the process depends on DynamoDB; between 11:48 PM and 2:24 AM, leases between DWFM and droplets slowly timed out.
ECS, EKS and Fargate began experiencing container launch failures and cluster scaling delays (lasting until 2:20 PM Oct 20).
Redshift query and cluster operations began failing while DynamoDB endpoints were down (lasting until 2:21 AM Oct 20; some clusters until 4:05 AM Oct 21).
AWS Support Center began experiencing issues; it failed over to another region as designed, but an account metadata subsystem returned invalid responses (lasting until 2:40 AM Oct 20).
Lambda began experiencing DynamoDB endpoint issues preventing function creation and updates and causing invocation errors (lasting until 2:15 PM Oct 20).
STS began experiencing API errors (recovered at 1:19 AM Oct 20, then errors again 8:31-9:59 AM Oct 20 due to NLB health check failures).
AWS Management Console sign-in began experiencing IAM user authentication failures due to DynamoDB issues (lasting until 1:25 AM Oct 20).
Amazon Connect began experiencing elevated errors handling calls, chats and cases (lasting until 1:20 PM Oct 20; second period from 7:04 AM Oct 20).
Engineers identified DynamoDB's DNS state as the source of the outage.
Temporary mitigations enabled some internal services to connect to DynamoDB and repaired key internal tooling, unblocking further recovery.
Redshift and ECS/EKS/Fargate recovery windows were tied to DynamoDB restoration; Redshift impact ended at 2:21 AM Oct 20.
Droplet leases between DWFM and droplets finished timing out (the lease-timeout period began at 11:48 PM Oct 19).
All DNS information was restored for DynamoDB; DWFM began re-establishing leases across the EC2 fleet, and EC2 APIs began returning 'insufficient capacity' errors for new launches.
New EC2 instance launches failed (period of impact for EC2 launches).
Customers could resolve the DynamoDB endpoint and connect as cached DNS records expired.
All global table replicas were fully caught up.
DynamoDB API error rates returned to normal (end of DynamoDB impact period).
Engineers throttled incoming work and began selective restarts of DWFM hosts, clearing queues and allowing leases to be established.
Lambda internal subsystem polling SQS queues was restored (it had failed and not recovered automatically).

DWFM had established leases with all droplets in us-east-1; new launches started to succeed, though many requests saw 'request limit exceeded' errors due to throttling. Network Manager also began propagating network configurations to newly launched instances, with a significant backlog.
Network Load Balancer (NLB) began experiencing increased connection errors for some load balancers (lasting until 2:09 PM Oct 20).
Network Manager latencies increased as it worked through the backlog; new instances could launch but lacked network connectivity. Engineers worked to reduce load on Network Manager.
Monitoring detected NLB health check issues caused by new EC2 instances being brought into service before network state had fully propagated; engineers began remediation.

From this point, NLB health check failures triggered Lambda instance terminations, leaving Lambda under-scaled; engineers throttled asynchronous work. Amazon Connect also saw a second period of errors from this time.

events.time: After 6:52 AM, shortly before 9:36 AM Oct 20 (PDT)
events.description: Degraded health check subsystem triggered automatic AZ DNS failover, taking multi-AZ load balancer capacity out of service and causing connection errors.
STS experienced a second period of API errors due to NLB health check failures (lasting until 9:59 AM Oct 20).
Engineers disabled automatic health check failover for NLB, bringing all healthy nodes and targets back into service and resolving connection errors.
Network propagation times returned to normal and new EC2 launches operated normally; launches began to succeed from this time.
EC2 launches began to succeed (some newly launched instances had connectivity issues until 1:50 PM Oct 20).
Engineers began relaxing EC2 request throttles.
STS recovered from its first period of API errors.
AWS Management Console sign-in IAM user authentication failures ended.
All EC2 APIs and new instance launches operating normally.
Automatic DNS health check failover for NLB was re-enabled after EC2 recovered; NLB connection errors ended.
Overall event ended (the report states the event ended at 2:20 PM on October 20); ECS, EKS and Fargate impact ended.
